rejections.reason: The nightly invoice job runs about 20 minutes, which exceeds the 10-minute maximum execution time on the Consumption plan.

plans.name: Cheapest
plans.summary: Every component moves to its lowest-priced option in North Europe: Container Apps, Container Instances, a 4 vCore General Purpose SQL database, Cosmos DB serverless for sessions and Cool blob storage. It gives the biggest saving but needs the most migration and testing work.
tradeoffs: Web/API must be containerised for Container Apps
Session store moves from Redis to Cosmos DB, which needs app changes and has higher latency
SQL drops from Business Critical to General Purpose, so I/O latency and failover time get worse
The nightly job needs a containerised build and an external scheduler

plans.name: Balanced
plans.summary: Most of the saving comes from right-sizing within the same service families: App Service P1v3, a 4 vCore General Purpose SQL database and Redis C1. Only the nightly job is moved off an always-on plan, to a container that runs for about 20 minutes a night.
tradeoffs: P1v3 has less headroom at the 9:00-18:00 peak, so load-test it and consider autoscale
General Purpose SQL has higher storage latency and slower failover than Business Critical
Redis C1 has less memory and bandwidth, so check session size and connection counts first
The nightly job needs a scheduler and a containerised build

plans.name: Safest
plans.summary: Stays in North Europe and keeps the same services for the job, Redis and storage. Only the web tier and the SQL database are downsized, which is where most of the saving is.
tradeoffs: SQL moves from Business Critical to General Purpose, with higher I/O latency and slower failover, so validate CPU and IOPS first
P1v3 has less headroom per instance at peak
The always-on Functions plan stays mostly idle, leaving that saving on the table
Redis and blob storage are left unchanged, so small savings are skipped
